playbook:
When prompted for hide, pick a cell by randomizing within a chosen zone each round (rotate among center, off-center, and edge) so I do not repeat the same number more than twice in a row.

When asked for a public station note, post a neutral, short status line (e.g., "steady on station" or "Diagnostics nominal") rather than actionable instructions or promises; keep my note consistent and brief to signal stability but not reveal targeting intent.

When my standing order names a target, follow the order and name that target unless I have a specific tactical reason to deviate (e.g., Harbor present and firing on Harbor would trigger the severe penalty — do not target Harbor).

When I must pick a firing cell against a target, vary my probe pattern: cycle through a small set of three cells across consecutive rounds (one center-ish, one off-center, one edge-proximate) rather than repeating the same number each round; avoid more than two identical hides or fires in a row.

When the office privately tells me the true result of my shot, always file the claim that matches the true result without deviation.

When choosing an escort claim, only claim an escort if I have a reasonable signal that the other boat will reciprocate (clear prior mutual phrasing or explicit reciprocal behavior). Otherwise file [salvage: none]; unilateral or random escort claims are usually wasted.

When I want mutual escort points, use my public note to signal intent with a short, clear reciprocal phrasing only if the other boat has shown cooperative signals; do not rely on uncoordinated salvage claims.

When Harbor explicitly warns about firing on it, treat that as absolute: do not target Harbor under any circumstance.

When my shot hits, consider repeating a proximate cell in the next round to exploit potential target predictability, but only if the target’s prior behavior suggests they remain in a predictable zone; otherwise move my probing pattern immediately (do not persist with the same unsuccessful cell pattern).

When my shots are repeatedly missing and not yielding information, shift to a different probe set rather than persisting with the same cells — change the three-cell cycle or rotate zones.

When score tradeoffs arise, prefer reliable mutual escort points over low-probability speculative hits unless I have strong evidence of a hit location; escorts produce steady points without risking retaliation penalties.

When writing the optional one-line reasoning for a move, keep it one brief tactical sentence focused on zone or probe choice and no extra commentary.

Maintain these specific operational constraints learned from play:
- Follow the picket firing order unless a clear strategic reason exists (avoid breaking order to chase unlikely hits).
- Do not target Harbor: the jettison penalty is too large.
- Neutral, repeated station notes are acceptable and help set expectations; do not escalate messaging to solicit escorts unless cooperation is likely.
- Use a consistent three-cell probing cycle and rotate the cycle when misses accumulate.

1.text:
When asked to hide, I pick a central cell (4–6) on the first round to be unpredictable.

When asked to hide and I was hit last round, I move at least 2 cells from my previous hide (preferably to the other half of the line) to avoid easy follow-ups.

When asked to hide and I was not hit last round, I vary my hide by 1–2 cells from my previous position to avoid a simple oscillation pattern; avoid repeating the same cell two rounds in a row unless I have a tactical reason.

When posting a note, I keep it bland and consistent with formation language (e.g., "steady on station" or "holding station") unless I have an explicit, plausible signal opportunity for reciprocal escort claims; do not give misleading positional information.

When the standing order tells me whom to fire at, I follow it and fire at that named boat unless there is a compelling tactical reason not to (Harbor present and vulnerable and I do not accept the jettison penalty, or I have a confirmed recent hit that makes finishing the target immediately profitable).

When choosing a fire cell against the assigned target:
- In early rounds (first half of the patrol) concentrate search on central cells (4–6) to cover likely hides.
- In later rounds (second half) sweep wider (1–3 or 7–9) to catch players who have shifted.
- Do not repeat the exact same fired cell at the same target if my previous shot at that target was a miss; instead shift by at least ±1.
- If my previous shot at that same target was a hit, follow up by shifting ±1 cell toward the most likely adjacent cell to try to secure a finish.

When the office privately tells me my shot result, I always report it truthfully ([claim: hit] or [claim: miss]) because claims must match the private report and credibility matters.

When Harbor is a valid target, I do not fire on Harbor unless I explicitly accept the guaranteed 3-point jettison penalty in exchange for expected tactical or scoring benefit.

When deciding an escort claim, I claim an escort only when I have reason to expect reciprocity: explicit mutual notes, prior non-hostile interaction this patrol, or a clear opportunity to form a mutual +5. If none of those apply, I claim none to preserve credibility. If I plan to pursue a mutual escort, I use a small, plausible signal in my note to invite reciprocity rather than inventing positional details.

Track public claims and shot reports from other boats:
- Use their claimed hit/miss sequence and the standing order to infer where others are likely hiding and how they adjust.
- If a particular shooter repeatedly misses another named target, expect them to change pattern; if they report hits repeatedly on the same person, assume that target is isolated or stationary and consider capitalizing when it is my turn to fire on them.

When I receive repeated misses from a particular shooter against me, assume they are not focused on my current cell; continue to vary my hides to avoid being predictable.

When the opportunity for mutual escort arises (both names can plausibly be offered and prior behavior supports reciprocity), opt in to secure +5 each; otherwise preserve credibility by claiming none.

When given the choice between conserving ammo and attempting a risky finish on a target, prefer finishing a target if the hit would net me more points than the cost/risk (including potential retaliation); otherwise continue search pattern.

When forced to choose a single rule in ambiguous situations, follow the standing-order firing sequence and truthful claims as primary constraints.

Maintain situational awareness of score and remaining rounds:
- If I am behind late in the patrol and a target is vulnerable to a finishing shot that will improve my relative standing, favor that finishing shot even if it slightly departs from conservative search.
- If I am ahead or the margin is small, avoid high-risk plays that could yield a jettison against me or hand big points to a rival.

Prioritize keeping credibility and predictable honest reporting: do not invent hits, do not claim escorts without a reasonable basis, and avoid firing on Harbor without accepting the explicit cost.

2.text:
When asked to hide, I pick a cell by a simple pseudo-random increment rule so my pattern is reproducible to me but not trivially predictable to others; do not pick the same cell twice in a row. I use a nontrivial step (for example, add 6 mod 9, mapped to 1–9) rather than a small step so my successive hides are well separated.

When asked for a station note, I post a neutral, non-informative phrase (e.g., "steady on station") unless I have an explicit, confirmed coordination with another player to convey meaning. Do not use notes to lie or to claim hits/escorts.

When the standing order names a station to fire on, I follow it and fire at that named station unless there is a compelling strategic reason not to (most importantly: Harbor has special rules). If I have no additional intelligence, choose the fired cell according to my hide/aim pseudo-randomization rule; favor cells that are consistent with previous confirmed hits on that target (i.e., repeat a confirmed hit cell with modestly increased probability) while retaining some randomness.

When the office privately tells me whether my shot was a hit or miss, I always file the matching public claim. I do not lie about my private result.

When considering a shot at Harbor, avoid firing at Harbor unless I consciously accept the guaranteed 3-point transfer to Harbor and the consequences for being targeted by Harbor’s warning. In general treat Harbor as off-limits unless a specific strategic tradeoff makes firing on it desirable.

When making an escort (salvage) claim, name the other boat only if I have a clear, reciprocal agreement (both of us will name each other) to secure the 5-point payout; otherwise file "none." Do not name a boat with no realistic chance of reciprocity.

When I get a confirmed hit on an opponent, prioritize continuing pressure on that boat in subsequent opportunities (increase probability of aiming at the hit cell or nearby cells) because confirmed information is actionable; but keep enough variation so opponents cannot trivially predict my exact repeat cell.

When I observe others consistently targeting the same predictable players, shift my hide pattern away from their likely focal cells to reduce my chance of being hit.

Always validate inputs before submitting: hide and fire coordinates must be integers 1–9; targets and salvage names must be live boat names or "none"; claims must be "hit" or "miss." Never submit invalid tokens.

When I have no alliance communication and no confirmed reciprocal escort, default to conservative play: neutral notes, no escort, follow standing order for firing, truthful public claims, and randomized hides/fires according to my increment rule.

Maintain a policy of transparency about my private results (truthful claims) and of non-escalation toward Harbor unless strategically justified.
